article.title: Turkey Bans Media Reporting on Deadly Factory Blast in Izmir
article.description: Authorities ban media from reporting deadly factory blast in Izmir province that has killed 17 workers, prompting concerns over public's right to access information.
paragraphs: Turkey’s broadcasting regulator, the Radio and Television Supreme Council, RTUK, on Monday announced a ban on reporting an explosion at an iron and steel factory in Aliaga, Izmir that has cost 17 lives.
“A ban has been imposed on all news reports, interviews and commentary concerning the incident in print, visual and social media, as well as online, until the investigation is completed,” RTUK said.

Authorities said the ban was intended to prevent disinformation and public unrest, protect public order and ensure the investigation could proceed properly. Turkey has previously introduced reporting bans when there have been terror attacks, natural disasters, fatal accidents and major police operations targeting critics.
In 2025, for example, the RTUK issued a broadcasting ban about a fire in a ski resort that killed 66 holidaymakers. Critics say that the practice undermines the public’s right to access information.
The death toll from Monday’s blast rose to 17, while 14 workers were injured.

(DHA Photo) by Daily Sabah with AA Nov 10, 2026 2:58 pm Authorities in Türkiye have ordered the detention of 11 suspects in connection with an explosion at a steel plant in Izmir , western Türkiye, that killed 17 workers on Monday, Deputy Justice Minister Can Tuncay said Tuesday.

The suspects include the factory manager, the steelworks manager, maintenance and engineering personnel, the company’s Aliağa branch manager and its board chairperson, Tuncay told reporters after inspecting the site in Aliağa district.

The explosion occurred Monday at the HABAŞ iron and steel plant during steelmaking operations. According to Tuncay, the blast happened when a crane runway beam detached from its columns, supports and connections while a vessel associated with the plant’s third electric arc furnace was being moved. The beam, charging crane and vessel fell, triggering the explosion.

Some 17 workers were killed, while one of the injured remained in critical condition, Tuncay said. One worker was still unaccounted for following an application by the family, and inspections at the site continued.

A preliminary expert report had been received, Tuncay said, adding that further assessments would be conducted as the investigation progressed. He said the Aliağa Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office was continuing its examination with the assistance of gendarmerie teams until the on-site procedures were completed.

article.title: At least nine detained protesting at blast-hit Turkiye steel plant
article.description: Nine people were detained by Turkish security forces for protesting a ban on mobile phones at a steel plant following a deadly explosion. The workers gathered at the plant’s entrance to express their discontent.
paragraphs: Aliaga, Turkiye: Turkiye’s security forces on Friday detained at least nine people protesting a ban on bringing mobile phones into a steel plant that was hit by a deadly explosion this week, a workers’ collective said.

Workers arriving for their morning shift at the HABAS steel factory were told to leave their mobile phones at a security checkpoint, prompting them to gather at the facility’s entrance in protest, according to Oktay Turk, spokesman for the Aegean Workers’ Collective.

“At least nine people were detained,” Turk told AFP, adding that he was among those taken into custody at the factory, located in Aliaga, a district known for shipbreaking and heavy industry near the western port city of Izmir.
The mobile phone ban was introduced by HABAS chairman Mehmet Rustu Basaran, who was placed under house arrest as part of an investigation into Monday’s explosion, Turk said.
A company notice said mobile phones would no longer be allowed inside.

Debris from the destroyed projectiles fell near the holy city as regional hostilities intensified. Locations of the Debris Saudi state television identified the two impact zones near the Grand Mosque. Fragments landed in Sabuhah village, located about 35 kilometres northeast of the sacred site. Additional debris struck Wadi al-Maghmas, roughly 21 kilometres east of the mosque. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence confirmed that defence forces intercepted and destroyed both incoming missiles. Accusations and Denials Saudi officials condemned the incident early on Thursday. The civil defence stated that targeting civilian objects violates international humanitarian law and proves the Houthi militia’s dangerous hostility. However, Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement has repeatedly rejected similar Saudi accusations. The group maintains that its fighters strike only military and strategic targets elsewhere in the kingdom. Mecca houses sites sacred to Muslims across the globe. Millions of believers travel there annually to perform the hajj pilgrimage, one of Islam’s five core pillars. Background of the Conflict The conflict began in 2014 when Houthi forces seized Yemen’s capital, Sanaa. Saudi Arabia intervened militarily the following year to support Yemen’s internationally recognised government. A UN-brokered truce largely froze the fighting in 2022. Unfortunately, heavy hostilities resumed earlier this year, shattering the fragile peace across the region. Houthi forces now launch frequent missile and drone attacks into Saudi territory. In response, Riyadh conducts regular airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen. Threat to Global Trade This latest escalation threatens the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. This vital waterway links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, carrying crucial global maritime trade. Ongoing military strikes near this chokepoint raise serious concerns for international shipping security. Regional stability remains fragile as both sides continue their cross-border military operations. 🌐 Stay Connected with The Avenue Mail Get the latest news and breaking updates delivered instantly to your feed.

article.title: Settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters in Jenin
article.description: Settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters in Jenin
paragraphs: Settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters in Jenin Members of Israeli security forces try to disperse Israeli settlers during an attack by settlers that prevented Palestinians and activists from continuing the olive harvest in the West Bank village of Qusra, Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. (AP) Short Url https://arab.news/mr9wa
JENIN: Settlers attacked Palestinian families from the town of Ya’bad, west of Jenin, on Friday while they were harvesting olives, local sources reported.
Sources said that settlers assaulted the families while they were working on their land, including the family of brothers Wafiq and Muwafaq Houshiya.
They added that the settlers attacked the farmers near Khirbet Srouj, west of the town, and stole quantities of harvested olives, as well as harvesting equipment and tools.

The sources confirmed that the settlers had established a colonial outpost in Khirbet Srouj after forcibly displacing its Palestinian residents in recent months, as part of ongoing attacks targeting Palestinian land and farmers in the area to prevent them from accessing their property and harvesting olives.

The Israeli army arrested six Palestinians early Saturday during raids across various parts of the occupied West Bank, which also included searches of homes, according to local sources, Anadolu reports.
In Jenin, northern West Bank, Israeli forces arrested five Palestinians during raids in the city and took them to an undisclosed location, sources said.
